params.message: steps up to the ATM terminal and makes a deposit.

chitchat: Colvane runs a thumb along a joint, finds something, and goes back over it.
She turns a shackle over twice, looks at the pin, and puts it in a different tray.
The kettle clicks off behind her. She does not turn round.
She writes a figure on a docket, looks at it, and writes a smaller one underneath.
Somewhere out in the hall a strap creaks as a hull settles a quarter inch into its cradle.
description: A short, heavy-shouldered woman in her forties in a boiler suit washed colourless. Her forearms are covered in small old burns and there's dirt under her nails. She keeps her hands where you can see them.

bye.text: "Right you are." She has the shackle back in her hand before you are through the door.

options.label: Let me see what you have.

carry.text:
"A patch kit, before anything." She taps the tin. "It's the difference between towing her home and driving her."

"The dinghy rolls up small enough to carry. Blow it up and you cross open water dry, which matters the day she sinks under you. The line and the cover are for the boat, not for you."

drop.text: "Not here." A pause exactly long enough to notice. "Slings are webbing and they get binned on a schedule, whatever they look like. That's their rule, not mine, and it's a good one. A wire sling tells you it's going by looking wrong for a month first. Webbing doesn't tell you anything at all."

fix.text: "Bring her in and I'll look." She nods at the slot. "Stand in here with me and refit, and she comes back sound, wherever you've got her lying in this yard. I'm in nine till six." "Out on the water you're on your own. With a patch kit on you, refit gets a split closed and her home. A patch won't take her past about half afloat, or most of the way if you're at a cradle. Past that it's shed work."

gossip.text:
"Nothing you'd call news." She thinks about it properly rather than dismissing it. "The Echelon moved. Week before last, middle of the night, out and back inside four hours. Nobody's meant to notice that and I notice everything on this water because it all comes past my end wall."

"Other than that: somebody's been taking a boat out of the hardstanding at night and putting it back. Covers go on wrong. Whoever it is, they're careful with it, which I mind less than I ought to."

hoist.text: "berth and her name, standing in here, and the hoist lifts her in." She holds up the pendant. "Two bays under this roof, one thousand six hundred to move in, and it's the only berth where I can put her right completely. berth on its own tells you what's free." "Four buttons. Up, down, that end, this end. There used to be eight and they took four off me, because somebody upstairs worked out that the other four were where the mistakes lived. They were right."

jobs.text: "Servicing, paint, a decal, a name." She counts them on the docket book. "All of it needs her under this roof: moored in here, or sat in the slot and stopped. Then refit service for oil, prop and a scrub of the bottom, refit paint, refit decal, or refit name. Not on a hire." "Oil goes with distance, the prop with whatever you hit, and the bottom grows weed while she sits afloat at a pontoon. All three slow her down. In here or up on a cradle, the weed stops."

options.label: Do you know who it is?

lapsed.text:
She does not look out at the hall, which is how you know she knows exactly which one you mean.

"Bay three. Two years in April." She squares the docket book against the counter edge. "Account's good. Pays on the day, every quarter, never a word with it."

"I check the straps on that one same as the rest. Turn the engine over twice a year. It'll start."

A beat.

"I'd rather they came and got it. But they're paying me to keep it ready, so I keep it ready, and what I think about it isn't on the docket."

lapsed_who.text:
"I know what's on the account." She lets that sit. "Which isn't the same as knowing, and it isn't mine to say either way."

"Ask me again when you've got a hull in here yourself. You'd be surprised what I'll tell somebody who's paying me."

owners.text:
"Halcyon own the water, the stone, the building and the glass." She counts none of it on her fingers. "They don't own the tools and they don't own me, and that took some arranging."

"They wanted the whole yard automatic. Showed me a machine that was going to do the lay-up. It did, as well. Beautifully. Then it did the next one exactly the same, and the next one after that, and a hull isn't a next one, it's whatever came in the door."

"So they kept the machine and they kept me. The machine does the covers."

options.label: What else can you do to her?
How do I get her under the roof?
Whose boat is the one nobody comes for?

root.text: "Afternoon." She puts down whatever she was holding, which not everybody does. "Anything with a hull in it, that's me. Buying and hiring are the desk, back through the lobby."

text_by_relation.familiar:
She has the kettle on before you have got the door shut, which is either hospitality or a diagnosis.

"Sit down. I know what you've done to it, I watched you come in."
text_by_relation.first:
The woman behind the counter finishes what she is doing before she looks up, and then looks up properly.

"Marit Colvane." She wipes a hand, considers it, and does not offer it. "I keep the hulls. Buying one, hiring one and the berth rate are the desk in the lobby, west through those doors, so don't come to me about the rate."

"If it floats and it's yours, I can lift it, park it, or fix it. Usually in that order."
text_by_relation.known: "You again." She is already reaching for the docket book. "Lift, park, or fix?"

visit.text: "Once a quarter, and never in the wet." She nods at the hall through the doorway. "They like it out there. Stand at the end by the dock, look at the water inside the building, say something about how it's the same level. It is the same level. That's the pumps, and the pumps are the only part of this place anyone has ever asked me about twice."

clothing_layers: a faded boiler suit with the sleeves pushed past the elbow
a rubber apron hanging loose, worn only at the bench
steel-capped boots gone pale with resin dust
a thermal layer underneath, because a glass building is a cold building

name: Marit Colvane
